stories.headline: Fake AI tools become new cyber threat as malware attacks on SMEs rise fivefold
stories.summary: Cyberattacks on small and medium-sized businesses (SMBs) have increased nearly fivefold, with 33,352 attacks detected between January and April 2026. These attacks involved malware or unwanted applications disguised as popular AI tools. Kaspersky's 2026 SMB threat report found a significant rise in such attacks, with a 39% increase compared to the same period in 2025. The report highlights the growing threat of fake AI tools being used to target SMBs. Cybercriminals are exploiting the popularity of AI services to spread malware, making SMBs attractive targets due to their often limited cybersecurity resources. The rise of AI-powered ransomware on the dark web further exacerbates the threat, with experts warning of the evolving nature of cyberattacks and the need for increased vigilance among SMBs to protect themselves from these emerging threats. The surge in attacks underscores the importance of robust cybersecurity measures for SMBs.

stories.headline: Google launches faster AI image, video tools to give users’ more creative powers
stories.summary: Google has launched faster AI image and video tools, giving users more creative powers. The new tools allow users to complete tasks such as image design and video editing through AI assistants, eliminating the need for separate apps. Google's Nano Banana 2, a new AI image generation model, brings enhanced features and faster image creation capabilities to a broader group of users. This model sits between speed and accuracy, offering many Pro-level capabilities without the need for expensive software. The tools will also provide images and videos to illustrate AI results, such as demonstrating objects or animals, making the results more engaging and informative. The launch is part of Google's effort to make AI content creation more widely available and user-friendly, aiming to deliver more accurate and helpful results to users.

stories.headline: Researchers discover novel SRV2 envelope protein for efficient CAR immune cell production
stories.summary: Researchers have discovered a novel SRV2 envelope protein that enhances the production of CAR immune cells, such as T and NK cells. The SRV2-based vector exhibits superior gene transduction efficiency, with approximately 20-25% higher CAR expression, compared to the commonly used RD114 vector. This breakthrough improves the production efficiency of CAR immune cell therapies, which are designed to recognize and destroy cancer cells. The SRV2 envelope protein facilitates more efficient transfer of anticancer genes into immune cells, leading to enhanced antitumor efficacy in mice. This innovation has the potential to significantly improve the scalability and effectiveness of next-generation cell and gene therapies, offering new hope for cancer treatment. The discovery was made by a Korean research team, which developed a new viral vector technology using the SRV2 pseudotyped retrovirus.

stories.headline: Apple Brings New Masking Tools to Final Cut Pro Amid Creator Studio Update
stories.summary: Apple has updated Final Cut Pro with new masking tools as part of the Creator Studio update. The professional video editing software now features powerful AI tools, including Generate Captions and Edit Detection. Additionally, new content such as Creator Themes with support for multiple aspect ratios, dynamic titles, and customizable options have been added. The update also brings new integrations with Pixelmator Pro, as well as other apps like Pages and Numbers. This update is part of the Apple Creator Studio subscription bundle, which was introduced in 2026 and includes access to Final Cut Pro, Logic Pro, Compressor, Main Stage, Motion, and Pixelmator Pro. The new tools and features aim to enhance creative workflows for visual creators, making it easier to produce high-quality video content. The update is available as part of the Apple Creator Studio subscription.

stories.headline: Nick Kyrgios hints at Wimbledon bow after foul-mouthed return
stories.summary: Nick Kyrgios has hinted that he may have played his last match at Wimbledon after a foul-mouthed outburst at an umpire during his return to the Championships. The incident occurred early in the second set of his match, in which he and partner Alexander Bublik were swiftly knocked out. Kyrgios' verbal spray at chair umpire Manuel Absolu could result in a fine of up to £37,000. Following the match, Kyrgios suggested that he had "probably" played his last match at Wimbledon, marking an emotional goodbye to his career at the All England Club. The Australian tennis player has a history of controversy and has previously been fined for his on-court behavior. Tournament officials are likely to review the incident and determine any potential disciplinary action. Kyrgios' comments have sparked speculation about his future participation in the tournament.

stories.headline: Celtics pry Mitchell Robinson away from Knicks on three-year deal
stories.summary: Mitchell Robinson has agreed to a three-year, $47.4 million contract with the Boston Celtics, ending his seven-year tenure with the New York Knicks. The deal, which includes a third-year player option, will be signed using the Celtics' full non-taxpayer mid-level exception. Robinson, the longest-tenured player from the Knicks' championship roster, helped the franchise capture its first NBA title since 1973. The 25-year-old center will now join the Celtics, bolstering their frontcourt. The signing is a significant move for Boston, adding a talented big man to their roster. Robinson's departure from the Knicks marks the end of an era, as he was a key contributor to the team's championship success. The Celtics' acquisition of Robinson is expected to strengthen their lineup and enhance their competitiveness in the league.

stories.headline: Harry Kane double rescues England in comeback win over DR Congo
stories.summary: England survived a huge scare against DR Congo, coming from behind to win 2-1 and secure a place in the World Cup last 16. DR Congo took the lead with their first international goal, scored by a 28-year-old player after a long ball from skipper Chancel Mbemba caught England's defense off guard. Despite England's dominance in possession, DR Congo's goalkeeper Lionel Mpasi made crucial saves to preserve the lead. However, Harry Kane scored two late goals to rescue England and seal the win. The victory sets up a last 16 clash with co-hosts Mexico. England's pressure eventually paid off, with Kane's double ensuring a dramatic comeback win in Atlanta. The Three Lions will now face Mexico in the next round, having overcome a significant challenge from the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

stories.headline: Italian Tresoldi targeted by Atletico Madrid for €30m swoop
stories.summary: Atletico Madrid is in negotiations to sign Nicolò Tresoldi from Club Brugge, with the Belgian club valuing the young striker at €30 million. Tresoldi, who is eligible to play for Italy or Germany, has impressed with his goal-scoring record and could potentially lead Italy's attack. The move comes as Atletico Madrid continues to strengthen its squad, despite recent reports of interest in other players, including Julian Alvarez and Oumar Solet. Atletico Madrid had previously rejected a €150 million offer from Real Madrid for Alvarez, demonstrating the club's commitment to its current squad and targets. Tresoldi's potential transfer is seen as a key move for Atletico Madrid, as the club looks to bolster its attacking options and compete at the highest level in European football. The negotiations are ongoing, with Atletico Madrid pushing to complete the deal.
